LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The top-level (global) scope of this PKGBUILD contains only ordinary variable assignments: pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, pkgdesc, arch, url, license, depends, optdepends, provides, conflicts, source, noextract, and sha256sums. There are no top-level command substitutions, `eval` statements, network fetches, or any code that executes at source time. The `source` array references only the package's declared upstream (github.com/rafatosta/zapzap) for its release artifacts, and checksums are recorded (not SKIPped).

The substantive logic — including a `$(sed ...)` command substitution and a heredoc that writes a launcher script — resides entirely inside the `package()` function, which `makepkg --printsrcinfo` does NOT invoke. Per the narrow scope of this gate, function bodies (pkgver, prepare, build, package) are out of scope and will be audited separately. Nothing in the top-level scope would execute attacker-controlled code, exfiltrate data, or download-and-run a payload when the PKGBUILD is sourced.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope contains only variable definitions; no executable risk.</summary>
</security_assessment>
